results.name: Director and Professor/Associate Professor Flathead Lake Biological Station, University of Montana
results.description:
The University of Montana (UM) invites applications for the position of Director and Professor/Associate Professor at the Flathead Lake Biological Station (FLBS). We seek a collaborative scientific leader to guide FLBS's internationally recognized programs in research, education, and outreach. The ideal candidate is an accomplished researcher who is excited to grow into a broader leadership role while advancing the FLBS’s mission and supporting faculty, students, staff, and research partners.

The Director of the Flathead Lake Biological Station lives in residence at FLBS as the chief academic and administrative officer of the Station and reports to the Vice President for Research at UM while maintaining a tenured appointment in a campus academic unit. The Director will provide visionary leadership to maintain and expand FLBS’s excellence in aquatic research, education, and outreach.

This position is a full-time, residential 12-month academic and administrative leadership appointment supported by an experienced associate director and administrative team. In addition to administrative duties at the station, the successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active research program and to engage in teaching consistent with the Director’s expertise, for example in FLBS’ summer session.

Please contact Robert Hall directly with any questions related to this posting, bob.hall@flbs.umt.edu or 307-690-6284. 

Key responsibilities include:

  • Strategic Leadership: Develop, articulate, and implement a clear strategic plan for FLBS that advances its mission, enhances its regional, national, and international prominence, and fosters innovation in aquatic research and education.

  • Research:  Develop and sustain an active and well-funded research program in their area of expertise including postdoctoral, graduate, and undergraduate mentoring.

  • Fundraising and Development: Lead major grant acquisitions and, with support from the FLBS’ development director, the UM foundation staff, and the FLBS Community Advisory Board, implement development efforts, campaigns, and fundraising initiatives to support FLBS programs, personnel, and infrastructure.

  • Research Development, Coordination, and Facilitation: Envision, coordinate, and/or facilitate FLBS research projects to ensure their smooth execution, including development of interdisciplinary collaborative projects within UM and beyond. 

  • Teaching: Contribute to educational mission by delivering, for example, a field-based course in the FLBS summer session.

  • Education and Training Program Oversight: Oversee and strengthen FLBS’ education, and training initiatives in coordination with UM departments and programs, ensuring integration with the university’s broader mission in support of undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral education and training, including research opportunities, summer field courses, and internships.

  • Community and External Engagement: Serve as a key representative of FLBS and provide information to stakeholders including government agencies, tribes, NGOs, community organizations, the public, and international partners. Support FLBS’ outreach programs, including the Flathead Lake Aquatic Research and Education K–12 program.

  • Faculty and Staff Development: Mentor, evaluate, and support faculty and staff, fostering a culture of collaboration and professional growth.

  • Financial Stewardship: Oversee the Station’s budget, facilities, and operations to ensure fiscal responsibility and sustainability.

  • Infrastructure and Facilities Oversight: Supervise the maintenance, improvement, and long term planning of FLBS’s physical plant, laboratory resources, and residential facilities to support long-term excellence.

 

Job Details

  • This is a 12-month, full-time academic and administrative leadership position at the rank of Associate or Full Professor with tenure in an appropriate UM academic unit and residence on-station at the Flathead Lake Biological Station.

  • As eligible and as appropriate, the successful applicant may be provided access to proceeds from the $1M Jessie Bierman endowment for discretionary use to advance research and educational activities at FLBS. 

  • Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications.

  • The University offers a competitive benefits package. including health insurance, retirement plans, paid leave, tuition benefits for employees and dependents, and professional development opportunities.

  • An outstanding record of sustained scholarly achievement in aquatic sciences involving ecological field studies

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills

  • Demonstrated aptitude for obtaining external funding

  • Experience in leading and managing research programs, budgets, facilities, and personnel

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ability to promote FLBS’ role as a global leader in aquatic research and education

  • Demonstrated commitment to collaborative, mission-driven leadership in support of research, education, and public service.

results.name: Director and Clinical Faculty, Graduate Program in Environmental Science and Natural Resource Journalism
results.description:
The School of Journalism at the University of Montana seeks a director for its master’s program in Environmental Science and Natural Resource Journalism. The two-year interdisciplinary degree combines journalism and science coursework to prepare students to report on environmental and natural resource issues across print, photo, video and multimedia platforms.

The director will provide strategic leadership and implement a vision for how the program will continue to prepare journalists to define coverage on a beat that impacts all facets of society and our world. They will lead recruitment and admissions, advise students through the curriculum, oversee the program's signature field projects, including the Crown Reporting Project and the Story Lab course, and represent the program to university leadership, donors and the professional journalism community. This is a full-time, benefited clinical faculty position that combines teaching, student mentorship and program administration.

Position Details

Title:  Director/Clinical Faculty

Salary: $60,000-$70,000 commensurate with experience
Schedule: Full-time, academic year position beginning August 2027
Benefits: Medical Insurance/Mandatory Retirement Contribution/Professional Development/Partial Tuition Waiver/Wellness
results.qualifications:
Required Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in journalism or a related field, the terminal degree for this position. In rare cases, substantial national-level professional journalism experience may be considered in lieu of the terminal degree.
  • Significant professional experience in journalism, with demonstrated strength in environmental or natural resource reporting.
  • Experience teaching or mentoring early-career journalists in a classroom, newsroom, or field setting.
  • Demonstrated record of producing or editing published or broadcast journalism covering environmental or natural resource topics.
  • Strong organizational, leadership and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with student advising, program administration, team leadership or related management responsibilities.
  • Ability to lead and advance a small graduate program while supporting student success and program growth.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior successful experience directing, coordinating or managing an academic program, newsroom or similar initiative.
  • Established professional network in environmental journalism, science communication or natural resource reporting.
  • Experience securing grants, fellowships, donor support or other external funding for journalism or academic programs.
  • Experience teaching multimedia storytelling, including audio, video, photography, data journalism or emerging digital storytelling approaches.
  • Experience working with Indigenous communities and/or reporting on tribal natural resource, environmental or sovereignty issues.
  • Familiarity with the issues and communities of the American West, including Montana's tribal nations, is desirable.
  • Commitment to fostering partnerships that support student learning, professional development and community engagement.

results.name: Assistant Professor of Video Journalism, School of Journalism
results.description:
The School of Journalism at the University of Montana seeks a tenure-track assistant professor to teach and help redesign the undergraduate multiplatform video storytelling track within the Bachelor of Arts in Journalism. This position will teach video reporting, interviewing, shooting, scripting, and editing. The position combines a full teaching load with responsibility for helping to design the future of video journalism.

The successful candidate will teach courses across our program, with an emphasis on video courses and skills. They will work with school leadership and faculty to define the video competencies all graduates should develop and will map them across courses that include lectures and hands-on learning and production. The successful candidate will help assess and develop the track's coverage of contemporary platforms, production practices, and emerging tools, including social and web video. The successful candidate will know and teach evolving digital technologies, with an eye toward guiding how those can be strengthened within course offerings. The Assistant Professor will expand and strengthen the track's applied learning opportunities, including the Student Documentary Unit and projects distributed through Montana PBS and other broadcasters. The successful candidate will also advise students, participate in school, college and university governance and service, and maintain an active record of professional practice, scholarship or creative work appropriate to a journalism faculty appointment.

Position Details

Tenure Track Faculty:  Assistant Professor of Video Journalism 
Schedule: Full time academic year position beginning fall semester 2027

Salary: $60,000-$70,000 per year commensurate with qualifications.
Benefits: Medical Insurance/Mandatory Retirement Contribution/Professional Development/Partial Tuition Waiver/Wellness

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with and reporting on communities representing a range of backgrounds and experiences.

results.name: Assistant Professor of Music Education, School of Music, Theatre, and Dance
results.description:
The University of Montana School of Music, Theatre, and Dance seeks a creative, collaborative music educator to prepare future elementary music teachers, instrumental music directors, and choral directors. Responsibilities include teaching introduction to music education, classroom instruments, general music methods for music majors, music in the classroom for elementary education majors, and other courses that match the chosen candidate’s strengths and the program needs.

In collaboration with faculty colleagues, the successful candidate will coordinate practicum placements, supervise field experiences, and support student teaching. The position also serves as a liaison between the School of Music, Theatre, and Dance and the College of Education. It is expected to maintain strong relationships with local and regional music educators, schools, and professional organizations.

As a tenure-track faculty member, the successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching, creative scholarship, and service. This position will also contribute to committees, meetings, auditions, and recruitment activities.

Position Details

Tenure Track Faculty: Assistant Professor

Salary: $55,000-$65,000 commensurate with experience
Schedule: Full-time, tenure-track academic year position beginning August 2027
Benefits: Medical Insurance/Mandatory Retirement Contribution/Professional Development/Partial Tuition Waiver/Wellness
results.qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in music and a minimum of five (5) years of successful elementary general music teaching experience.
  • Training and/or certification in one or more recognized music teaching approaches (e.g., Orff, Kodaly, Dalcroze, Feierabend, Gordon) is expected.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctorate in music education.
  • Experience working in a variety of teaching settings.
  • A record of effective college-level teaching.
  • Developing or established record of scholarly activity.
  • Experience in emergent areas (e.g., popular music pedagogies, world music pedagogies, culturally responsive/sustaining pedagogies, etc.)
  • Knowledge and ability to use current interactive technology (including AI), as a tool for teaching in multiple learning modalities.

results.description:
The University of Montana, School of Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Science (UMPT), within the College of Health, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor for the Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program to begin August 2027.

 

The DPT program is for a fully CAPTE-accredited 2.75-year entry-level program with 36 students per class. It is the only Physical Therapy program in the state and has been CAPTE-accredited for over 40 years.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Teaching and advising students in the DPT program
  • Establishment of an active research agenda. Numerous opportunities for collaborative research are available within the School, College, and University, as well as with other clinical partners, and healthcare institutions
  • Service on department and university committees as well as the profession
  • Instructional needs may include:
    • Clinical Medicine series (pathophysiology, medical screening, pharmacology, special populations), and
    • Physical therapy management coursework in musculoskeletal and complex/acute care patient populations

The instructional load for the position will align with your expertise and interest and be consistent with other tenure-track faculty of the same rank. Teaching content is negotiable, and flexibility will be possible to balance your interests with the needs of the program.

results.name: Postdoctoral Research Associate, Computer Science
results.description:
The University of Montana invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate for Computer Science. The associate will conduct computational research for the NSF-funded project Collaborative Research: CAIG: Uncertainty-aware Physics-informed Machine Learning of Ice Calving and Sliding.

The position will develop, test, and apply fast differentiable ice sheet models that combine physical constraints with machine learning to improve representations of basal sliding and iceberg calving and to quantify uncertainty in glacier projections. The work will emphasize GPU-accelerated modeling and will investigate physics-informed neural networks and universal differential equations as complementary approaches. 

The associate will work with the University of Montana project team and Dartmouth collaborators on model development, numerical experiments, uncertainty analysis, publications, and open research software. Case studies are expected to include Jakobshavn Isbræ, Helheim Glacier, and Kangerlussuaq Glacier in Greenland. 

This is a grant funded position guaranteed for two years.

 

Examples of Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develop and evaluate GPU-accelerated and differentiable glacier and ice-sheet models. Implement physics-informed machine learning approaches for basal sliding and calving, including PINNs, UDEs, and related hybrid methods. Extend project software to support time-dependent evolution and moving glacier fronts
  • Design and run numerical experiments for Greenland outlet glacier case studies. Integrate observational and model data, evaluate performance against appropriate benchmarks, and diagnose physical and numerical behavior
  • Develop and apply uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis workflows. Propagate uncertainty in learned sliding and calving relationships into glacier and sea level projections through 2100
  • Communicate and disseminate results through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, documentation, and reproducible open-source software. Participate in project meetings and, as appropriate, mentor students and contribute to proposal development
results.qualifications:
• A PhD completed by the start date in computer science, glaciology, geophysics, applied mathematics, engineering, or a closely related field
  • Research experience in computational modeling of glaciers, ice sheets, or closely related geophysical systems
  • Experience with machine learning and at least one scientific machine learning approach, such as physics-informed neural networks, differentiable programming, neural operators, universal differential equations, or hybrid physics- and data-driven modeling
  • Proficiency in scientific programming using Python, Julia, or a comparable language and experience developing, testing, and maintaining research code
  • Ability to use GPU or high-performance computing resources for numerical modeling or machine learning workloads
  • Ability to formulate research questions, design computational experiments, evaluate model behavior, and communicate results in writing and presentations
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and multi-institutional research team

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience modeling marine-terminating glaciers, Greenland outlet glaciers, basal sliding, iceberg calving, or moving-boundary problems
  • Experience with PINNs, UDEs, neural operators, graph neural networks, convolutional networks, transformers, or related architectures for scientific problems
  • Demonstrated experience using remote sensing, geospatial, or other Earth observation data in model calibration or evaluation
  • Experience with GPU-oriented frameworks or tools such as JAX, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Julia GPU packages, CUDA, or comparable technologies
  • Experience with Bayesian methods, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, ensemble methods, or probabilistic modeling
  • Evidence of peer-reviewed publication, collaborative research, open-source software contribution, or student mentoring

results.name: Dean, Mansfield Library
results.description:
The University of Montana invites applications for an imaginative and collaborative leader to serve as Dean of the Maureen and Mike Mansfield Library. Reporting directly to the Provost and Vice President of Academic Affairs, the dean serves as the library’s chief academic and administrative officer.

This position offers the opportunity to shape the future of an essential academic and cultural resource at a public research university that combines R1 research excellence with a deep commitment to student success and service to Montana. The next dean will work with library employees, students, faculty, and campus and community partners to develop a shared vision that strengthens the library’s contributions to learning, research, and creative scholarship.

Building on the Mansfield Library’s distinctive collections, expertise, services, partners, and history of adaptation, the dean will champion broad and equitable access to knowledge while anticipating the changing needs of the university and the communities it serves. Opportunities include advancing information and AI literacy, guiding the thoughtful adoption of emerging technologies, and expanding partnerships that connect the library’s resources and expertise with teaching, discovery, and public engagement. The university seeks a leader who inspires trust, supports and develops library employees, and builds the relationships and resources needed to translate a shared vision into meaningful outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop a future-facing shared vision of the Library through a collaborative process that aligns with UM institutional mission and grounding in shared governance and UM’s institutional mission
  • Guide the establishment of administrative structures, shared services integration, and internal communication frameworks
  • Represent the Library in campus-wide planning and decision-making, and externally to alumni, donors, government agencies, shared governance, and professional partners
  • Advance the academic mission and evolving strategy of the library, including internal consultation and external communication
  • Engage faculty, departments, and service units in articulating a mission and vision that reflects the Library’s role in fostering critical inquiry, cultural understanding, civic leadership and meeting their teaching, learning, research and scholarship needs
  • Partner with the Vice President for Student Success and Enrollment Management, and other administrative offices to strengthen visibility to support student retention, learning, research, and wellness
  • Steward fiscal resources responsibly and in ways that are aligned with the University mission and vision, with consideration for and participation in the wider MUS library system strategy.
  • Support graduate education through alignment of teaching and research support
  • Lead faculty and staff hiring and development, including workload oversight and promotion/tenure processes, in accordance with University policy and Collective Bargaining Agreement
  • Partner with the UM Foundation to initiate philanthropic engagement and support
  • Contribute to institutional priorities as an Academic Officer, advising the Provost on strategic planning, assessment, and academic operations

results.description:
The Department of Forest Management (DFM) in the W.A. Franke College of Forestry and Conservation at the University of Montana invites applications for a full-time academic year tenure-track Assistant Professor of Silviculture. The candidate will advance the DFM’s mission to provide innovation and leadership in the use of active forest management to achieve beneficial ecological and socioeconomic outcomes. This mission includes educating future forestry professionals, engaging in cutting-edge research to solve real-world problems, and contributing outward facing service to the discipline of forestry. The DFM welcomes applications from individuals with diverse perspectives and backgrounds. We encourage applications from veterans, women, persons of color, indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities and other individuals who can contribute to our intellectual diversity and cultural richness.

The successful candidate will develop an extramurally funded research program and demonstrate a commitment to translating their research into applications relevant to contemporary forest management. The College’s Lubrecht Experimental Forest offers a distinctive opportunity for field-based silvicultural research, teaching, and demonstration, and candidates are encouraged to consider how this resource could support the growth of their program. Teaching responsibilities include contributions to the Society of American Foresters accredited professional B.S. Forestry curriculum. Specific courses to be taught include undergraduate and graduate courses in silviculture as well as other courses as assigned. The successful candidate will mentor graduate students at the MS and PhD level and contribute to undergraduate advising and mentoring. The successful candidate will engage in relevant service within the forestry discipline, as well as service to the department, college, and university which is expected to be scaled upon establishment of productive research and teaching programs.

For detailed information regarding faculty duties and expectations, please contact the Search Chair, Andrew Larson a.larson@umontana.edu, to request a copy of the Dept. of Forest Management Unit Standards. 

Position Details

Title: Assistant Professor of Silviculture
Schedule: Full-time academic year position beginning fall semester 2027

Salary: $70,000-$85,000 per year commensurate with qualifications

Benefits: Medical Insurance/Mandatory Retirement Contribution/Professional Development/Partial Tuition Waiver/Wellness 

 

About Us

The Department of Forest Management comprises a multidisciplinary faculty focused on developing the foundation and tools necessary for sustainable management of forest landscapes. DFM occupies a unique position in FCFC as steward of a nationally accredited professional degree in Forestry that has served students since 1913. DFM members are active in basic and applied research with noteworthy productivity in fire and water sciences, remote sensing, biometrics, forest and fire ecology, and silviculture. DFM faculty direct the Montana Climate Office, the National Center for Landscape Fire Analysis, and the Wilderness Institute, each with significant outlays in infrastructure, grants and contracts, staff, and graduate students. DFM’s teaching, research, and outreach are enhanced by Lubrecht Experimental Forest and Bandy Ranch, both located within easy driving distance of campus in the Blackfoot Valley. FCFC is highly interdisciplinary and has multiple programs that promote collaboration across departments in both teaching and research. Additional information about the college can be found at https://www.umt.edu/environment/.

results.description:
The joint immunology lab of Drs. Blair DeBuysscher and Jay Evans at the University of Montana is seeking a Post Doctoral Scientist to join our pioneering research in developing novel vaccines. Join our immunology team and play a pivotal role in the advancement of next-generation vaccines. We're looking for driven individuals passionate about understanding the mechanism of action around innovative adjuvants and vaccines. Ideally, candidates will possess a robust understanding of multiomic approaches and bioinformatics. Proficiency in immunology, flow cytometry, and mouse handling would be highly advantageous.

Our multidisciplinary team is dedicated to exploring innovative strategies at the convergence of immunology, formulation science and chemistry, to tackle challenges in vaccine design and development. We are a well-funded, collaborative research team with strong connections in academia and industry. Our team is at the forefront of vaccine research, focusing on a range of diseases impacting human health, including tuberculosis, COVID-19, monkeypox, Lyme disease, Flu, RSV, and opioid addiction. Additionally, we delve into understanding host-pathogen interactions, immunopathology, and immune-mediated protection at the molecular level. Apply and become a part of our team of creative and forward-thinking scientists in beautiful Montana.

results.description:
The Center for Translational Medicine at the University of Montana, Missoula MT, is seeking a postdoctoral research scientist to join the collaborative lab of Drs. Blair DeBuysscher and Jay Evans. Be a part of our interactive and multidisciplinary research team dedicated to pioneering the discovery and development of innovative vaccines. Our focus spans a wide spectrum of diseases affecting human health, including COVID-19, influenza virus, tuberculosis, pertussis, and opioid addiction. Additionally, we study the molecular intricacies of host-pathogen interactions, vaccine-mediated immunity, and their impact on immunopathology and immune-mediated protection.

 

Join our multidisciplinary team and play a pivotal role in the advancement of next-generation adjuvants and vaccines. We're looking for driven individuals passionate about designing and developing innovative adjuvants and vaccines. Ideally, candidates will possess a robust understanding of immunology or molecular biology, along with hands-on experience in techniques crucial for investigating cell-mediated immunity, cell signaling, and receptor/ligand interactions. Proficiency in mouse handling, flow cytometry, and bioinformatics analysis would be highly advantageous. Embark on a new journey and become a part of our team of creative and forward-thinking scientists in beautiful Montana. Nestled amidst stunning landscapes, our research environment offers not only groundbreaking scientific opportunities but also an unparalleled quality of life.

Position details

  • Position is full-time, 1.0 FTE, Letter of Appointment and includes a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including insurance, mandatory retirement plan, partial tuition waiver, and wellness program.
  •  Salary for this position is consistent with NIH pay scales, starting $61,008.
